title: Evicting children from a parent's own property - an underused remedy
p1:
Can parents really remove their own children from their house? Many people are surprised to learn that the answer can be yes in certain situations.

A common belief is that once a child starts living in a parent's property, the parent loses control over it. That is not always true.
p2:
In many cases, senior citizens and parents facing harassment, neglect, or misuse of their property can seek legal remedies to protect their peaceful possession. The law recognizes that ownership rights do not disappear simply because the person causing trouble is a family member.

A lesser-known point is that parents may approach authorities or tribunals under senior citizen protection laws in appropriate cases to seek relief, including removal of children from their property.
p3:
This remedy is not about breaking family bonds. It is about protecting dignity, safety, and the right to live peacefully in one's own home.

Many parents tolerate years of distress because they do not know that legal options exist. Knowing your rights can help you take timely action instead of waiting for situations to become unbearable.
conclusion: Do you think more parents should be aware of their legal right to seek protection from misuse of their own property?
